issues.failure_explanation: By the displayed definition, the off-diagonal entries of the matrix of $\Delta_h$ equal $+1/h^2$, so they are positive, not negative. The sign condition is the stated premise for the $L_0$-type and stability conclusion, and from which the $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ convergence of the truncated Euclidean scheme is then asserted. As written, the inference starts from a false premise. It would only work for $-\Delta_h$.

failure_location.quote: observing that the off-diagonal elements of the discrete matrix associated with the discrete FDM system~\eqref{eq:FDM} are all negative, the ODE system is described by an $L_0$-type matrix

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the argument to $-\Delta_h$, which has non-positive off-diagonal entries and a positive diagonal, or replace the argument with the energy (dissipativity) argument used later in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The illustrative stability and convergence claim for the Euclidean truncated scheme in Section 2.3 is unsupported as stated. No later formal result depends on it.
issues.title: Sign of off-diagonal entries and L0-matrix stability claim for the Euclidean scheme
issues.why_classification: A local sign and wording correction in an illustrative section restores the claim. No result or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Summing up these relations for $k\in \overline{0,(k_{\tau,T}-1)}$, where $k_{\tau,T}=\left\lfloor \frac{T}{\tau}\right\rfloor$
Moreover, if $\theta=\frac{1}{2}$ (i.e., when we use the Crank-Nicolson scheme) and $T$ is an integral multiple of $\tau$, then the order of the convergence above is $\mathcal{O}(h^2+\tau^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop is repeat-until: it executes an update, increments $k$, and stops only once $k\tau>T$. If $T=K\tau$, then after $K$ updates $k\tau=T$ is not $>T$, so one more update is performed. The output therefore approximates $u((K+1)\tau)$, and in general $u(\lfloor T/\tau\rfloor\tau+\tau)$, rather than $u(T)$. The proof of the convergence theorem instead analyses $\lfloor T/\tau\rfloor$ steps. The extra step adds an error of size $\tau\sup\|\partial_t u\|$. With $\theta=1/2$ and $\tau=h$, this is $\mathcal{O}(h)$, so the output does not have the advertised $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ accuracy.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Run exactly $k_{\tau,T}=\lfloor T/\tau\rfloor$ updates, for example by stopping when $(k+1)\tau>T$, and require $T/\tau\in\mathbb{N}$ for the Crank-Nicolson rate. This matches the analysis in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the algorithm's output for $\theta=1/2$ is only $\mathcal{O}(h)$-accurate at time $T$. This contradicts the paper's claim that Algorithm 1 converges at $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ for every $\theta\in[1/2,1]$ in the Crank-Nicolson case. Theorem thm:convergence-theta itself, which analyses $\lfloor T/\tau\rfloor$ steps, is unaffected.
issues.title: Stopping rule overshoots final time, destroying the claimed Crank-Nicolson rate
issues.why_classification: Changing the termination condition is a one-line local fix. It restores the theorem's guarantee and rates without any new argument.
